claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has limited amorphous retention under rapid quenching.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits multiple, broad, or otherwise complicated crystallization or exothermic events during reheating.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve the alloy's thermal stability during reheating.
The boron intervention will remain effective at both high and moderately high quench rates.
Boron has a small atomic size relative to the metallic constituents of the alloy.
Boron has strongly negative mixing enthalpies with the metallic species in this alloy.
Boron addition increases atomic packing frustration in the liquid.
Boron addition increases local chemical disorder in the liquid.
The increased disorder slows crystalline-phase nucleation during cooling and reheating.
Boron addition increases the liquid viscosity.
Boron-induced viscosity and atomic-size mismatch suppress crystalline nucleation kinetics.
Suppressed nucleation produces a more uniformly amorphous structure after rapid quenching.
Suppressed nucleation delays or reduces crystallization during subsequent heating.
The boron-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous phase fraction across a wider range of cooling rates than the undoped alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit either a single better-defined crystallization event or a delayed crystallization onset during reheating.
The DSC response of the boron-modified alloy will be less complicated than that of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Boron additions above approximately 3 at.% may promote undesirable boride phases.
Boron-induced boride phases could compromise ductility and toughness.
At very slow cooling rates, equilibrium crystallization may prevail despite boron addition.
